I found the likely counterpart: [Vietnam Partner JSC](https://crm.example.test/#/companies/01a21855-9d50-76a6-9ea6-30618f86c073), with [Mai Nguyen](https://crm.example.test/#/contacts/01a21855-9e80-74af-b4af-9aab55dde362) as the sole recorded contact.

Calendar caveat: no calendar is connected, and there is no CRM-recorded meeting for Friday, November 27. I therefore can’t confirm the time or attendees.

Meeting brief:

- Mai wrote on November 6: “Thank you — we will review the appendix this week.”
- Your November 8 email promised to send a breakdown by the end of that week. Confirm whether it was delivered and reviewed.
- There are no deals, open pipeline, formal partner terms, or recorded meeting focus. The company status is “unknown.”
- Both records belong to Sofia Meier, not you.

Suggested objective: close the appendix/breakdown loop and qualify whether there is a real partnership opportunity.

A clean opening:

> “Mai, good to finally meet. I’d like to start with your review of the appendix and clarify whether you received everything you needed from our side. Then I’d like to understand what a useful partnership would look like for you and agree on concrete next steps.”

Questions to prioritize:

- What stood out—or remained unclear—in the appendix?
- Did you receive the promised breakdown?
- What partnership model are you considering?
- Which customers, market segments, or use cases would you target first?
- Who else participates in approval?
- What would a successful first 90 days look like?
- What concrete next step and owner can we agree before ending?

Main risk: the CRM is extremely thin, so avoid assuming commercial alignment. Treat this as a discovery and requalification meeting.
